label: inferable
contract: A column is as wide as the longer of its header and its widest cell, so a long header keeps the column separators lined up.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
for headers, rows, want in ((["product", "n"], [["tea", "4"], ["jam", "9"]], [8]), (["k", "description", "v"], [["a", "short", "x"]], [2, 16])):
    got = render_table(headers, rows)
    lines = got.split("\n")
    seps = [[i for i, ch in enumerate(lines[1]) if ch == "+"]]
    seps += [[i for i, ch in enumerate(line) if ch == "|"] for line in lines[:1] + lines[2:]]
    assert all(s == want for s in seps), (headers, rows, got)
heldout_check:

label: arbitrary
contract: With no rows, the table is the header line followed by the separator line.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
for headers in (["name", "qty"], ["id"]):
    got = render_table(headers, [])
    lines = got.split("\n")
    assert len(lines) == 2, repr(got)
    assert [cell.strip() for cell in lines[0].split("|")] == headers, repr(got)
    assert set(lines[1]) <= set("-+") and lines[1].count("+") == len(headers) - 1, repr(got)

label: arbitrary
contract: Cells holding int or float values are right-aligned in their column; all other cells, including strings of digits, are left-aligned.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["sku", "qty", "cost"], [["fig", 3, 1.5], ["42", 120, 10.25]])
assert [line.rstrip() for line in got.split("\n")] == [
    'sku | qty | cost',
    '----+-----+------',
    'fig |   3 |   1.5',
    '42  | 120 | 10.25',
], got
heldout_check:
